🇲🇽🌊 <u>12 YEARS AFTER GRUPO MÉXICO’S TOXIC SPILL, SONORA RIVER CLEANUP ENTERS PHASE TWO</u>

Semarnat chief Alicia Bárcena launched the second remediation stage in Ures for the basin hit in 2014 by 40 million liters of acidified copper sulfate from the Buenavista del Cobre mine — a disaster that poisoned 8 municipalities and 22,000 people while the old regime looked away. This phase targets soil recovery and water-quality monitoring. Bárcena: “No están solos, venimos a escucharlos e informarles con toda transparencia.”

🇲🇽🌎 <u>COLOMBIA SNUBS MEXICO’S RESCUE BRIGADE — ACCEPTS ONLY RIGHT-WING ALLIES</u>

With 224 dead after the 7.4 earthquake, President De la Espriella’s government took rescuers only from the US, Israel, Ecuador and El Salvador. Mexico’s Sedena brigade — among the most experienced earthquake rescue teams on the planet — was blocked on a paperwork pretext. Sheinbaum: “Están certificados, pero ahora piden otra certificación.” Mexico sent 58 tons of humanitarian aid anyway. That’s the difference between solidarity and ideology.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>ALITO’S INNER CIRCLE KEEPS FALLING: EX-AIDE HELD FOR $36M EMBEZZLEMENT</u>

Carlos Alberto Medina Hernández, former communications director in Campeche during Alejandro “Alito” Moreno’s governorship, has been detained for the alleged embezzlement of 36 million pesos. Prosecutors are mapping a peculado network built around the PRI leader’s years in power. The impunity shield that protected Alito’s Campeche operation is cracking, one collaborator at a time.

‍WSJ: Mexico Pushes for Lower Auto Tariffs in Trade Talks August 13, 2026 | 🟢 📰 WSJ exclusive: Mexico's USMCA counteroffer — apply the 25% auto tariff only to non-North-American content, cutting the effective rate to 5–10% for qualifying vehicles. It's the answer to a US demand for 50% US-made content that automakers themselves call unworkable. A fourth negotiating round is set for September; automakers warn they'll pull their cheapest models from the US market without a deal. (Paywalled — analysis from the headline, subhead and wire reprints.) • "apply levies on only a small portion of a car's value" • "potentially lowering final tariffs for many vehicles"

‍🇲🇽 NO US COVERAGE: Homicides down 51% since Sheinbaum took office — July lowest in 12 years August 11, 2026 | 🔍 📰 Tuesday's mañanera: homicides down 51% since October 2024 — from 86.9 to 42.5 per day, 44 fewer murders daily; July was the lowest figure in 12 years. Of 30,000+ weapons seized, around 80% came from the US. US outlets that covered cartel indictments and avocado halts this week: silent. 🔍 Guanajuato is down 76%, Guerrero 61%; over 63,500 arrests. Only Mexican English-language media reported the figures. • "homicides have fallen 51%, from 86.9 to 42.5 per day" • "around 80% come from the U.S."

‍THE GUARDIAN: The US tried to stop cartel money-laundering. It devastated mom-and-pop businesses instead August 11, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Guardian: Trump's FinCEN dropped the cash-reporting threshold from $10,000 to $200 across 30 border zip codes — billed as anti-cartel. It emptied casas de cambio, spooked immigrant customers, and buried grocers in paperwork. Courts have already blocked it in California and for plaintiffs in Texas and Arizona. Remittances to Mexico run near $60bn a year; owners say real launderers don't wire $300 at a grocery store. • "I don't think it was to prevent money laundering" • "They buy gold, they buy real estate, they buy cars"

‍CBS/AFP: Powerful cartel in Mexico sought to buy weapons overseas in exchange for fentanyl and meth, U.S. says August 12, 2026 | 🟢 📰 CBS runs the DOJ indictment straight: four alleged CJNG members tried to buy machine guns and RPG launchers in Czechia — paying in fentanyl and meth. Every source is a US agency. Two ironies the piece states without pausing on: this time the guns aren't American, and the alleged new CJNG boss was born in Santa Ana, California. The case sits inside the wider campaign — $100M+ in rewards, 50 sanctioned entities, El Mencho's February killing with US intelligence support. • "the defendants paid in the form of fentanyl and methamphetamine" • "President Trump has ramped up pressure on Mexico"

text: ‍REUTERS: Taylor Farms outbreaks show limits of U.S. ability to safeguard produce from Mexico August 13, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Reuters investigates the Taylor Farms outbreaks — 6,300+ cyclospora cases, two deaths — and lands on the FDA: staffing cut 22% since 2024, foreign inspections down 13% as imports from Mexico rose. For once the failure is Washington's oversight, not framed as Mexico's filth. Mexico now supplies over 20% of US food imports — up 1,500% since NAFTA — and a Mexican food-safety expert is quoted directly. • "Without question, the cuts are harmful to food safety" • "the United States is increasingly relying on Mexico's produce industry"

🇲🇽📈 <u>CITI: 2% GDP IN 2027 IF T-MEC HOLDS AND INFRASTRUCTURE PLAN EXECUTES</u>

Citi's chief economist for Mexico, Julio Ruiz, projects 2% GDP growth in 2027 — on two conditions: the T-MEC gets extended another 16 years and Sheinbaum's Infrastructure Plan is visibly executed. Miss either and the forecast drops.

Citi sees the US growing 1.8%, which Ruiz called "more than enough to keep pulling Mexican exports." Even Wall Street's roadmap for Mexico runs through the T-MEC and Plan México. (El Economista)
